column1: # milestone-driver - golden matrix for scripts/triage-cache.{sh,ps1} (issue #441).
# One row per READ-ONLY case. Columns, TAB-separated:
#   name         case label, reported on failure
#   args         the script's argv, SPACE-separated. No argument in this table
#                contains a space, and the runners disable globbing before the
#                split, so the column stays a plain word list.
#   stdout_file  golden under fixtures/triage-cache/_expected/. An EMPTY column
#                means "expect EMPTY stdout"; a NAMED-BUT-MISSING golden is
#                FATAL, never a silent degradation to "expect empty".
#   want_exit    expected exit code
#   stderr_file  golden under _expected/ for stderr; __SCRIPT__ inside it expands
#                to this leg's script filename, so ONE table drives both legs
#                while each asserts its OWN usage text. An EMPTY column means
#                expect EMPTY stderr, so those rows END IN A TAB (same
#                empty-last-column convention as resolve-citation.cases.tsv).
# The `write` subcommand has no row here: it MUTATES its root, so a committed
# fixture cannot express it. Both runners drive it from mktemp workspaces in
# bespoke blocks after this table.
# Paths are relative to tests/fixtures/triage-cache/, which both runners cd into,
# so no output text is checkout-dependent.
# name
query-keys-dedup
query-edges
query-no-numbers
query-bad-kind
query-bad-number
query-bad-owner
unknown-subcommand
lookup-wrong-argc
# The cache is READ from the canonical path, and from the legacy root ONLY when
# the canonical one is ABSENT. These two rows share one golden on purpose: the
# fallback must return the SAME answer, not merely some answer.
lookup-key-match
lookup-legacy-root-only
# roots/both holds BOTH files, with DIFFERENT contents: the canonical file knows
# issue 9 and the legacy one knows issue 7. A canonical-wins read reports issue 7
# as no-entry; a read that merged, or that preferred the legacy file, could not.
lookup-both-present
# A corrupt canonical file degrades to an EMPTY cache - it does NOT fall through
# to the legacy root, which here holds a file that would have produced a HIT.
# Same golden as the cache-absent row: both are the empty-cache answer.
lookup-bad-json
lookup-cache-absent
lookup-null-issue
lookup-no-aliases
lookup-malformed-response
lookup-missing-response
# WRONG-TYPED containers (comments/labels as numbers, a label node that is a bare
# string) degrade to the field defaults rather than aborting. This row is the twin
# pin: jq errors where the pwsh leg returns null, so before the obj/arr guards the
# .sh leg answered SKIP bad-response for this response while the .ps1 leg answered
# HIT. The cached keys ARE the degraded keys, so a HIT proves both legs built the
# same key text, not merely the same record shape.
lookup-wrong-typed-fields
# COLLATION (issue #471). The label set holds an astral name (U+1F600) beside a
# U+E000-FFFF one (U+FF21). UTF-16 code-unit order puts the astral name FIRST (its
# lead surrogate is U+D83D); codepoint / UTF-8 byte order puts it LAST. The cached
# key is the codepoint order the .sh leg's jq `sort` yields, so a HIT on both legs
# is the parity proof. Every other row here is ASCII, and ASCII agrees under both
# orders, so no other row can catch this.
lookup-astral-vs-bmp-labels
# Edge 100 is CLOSED/NOT_PLANNED, so both cached entries that reference it are
# downgraded. Edge 101 is CLOSED/COMPLETED - merged, and never a downgrade.
check-edges-closed-not-merged
check-edges-all-open
# roots/both's entry references edge 102 ONLY, whose stateReason is null: absent
# is not COMPLETED, so it is closed-but-not-merged and downgrades.
check-edges-null-state-reason
check-edges-empty-cache
check-edges-bad-json-cache
check-edges-bad-response
check-edges-missing-response
